problem: Multiple chats and agents can create repeated branch-head movement, duplicated CI waves, hot-file contention and generic test execution even when development work itself is parallel.
root_cause: Parallel agent execution was already modeled, but candidate writing, capability routing, risk classification, late-bound closure and bounded daily tuning were not combined into one executable engineering control loop.
prevention_rule: Parallelize specialist work before GitHub, keep one integrated candidate writer, select impacted tests and risk profiles, late-bind shared closure files, route agents by proven capability outcomes and tune only bounded performance parameters daily through protected delivery.
prevention: Impact graph and R0-R4 risk class before expensive execution.
Capability and outcome based specialist routing.
Daily bounded optimizer driven by CI telemetry.
No daily optimizer action may weaken security, Required, exact-SHA, protected merge or production readback.
failed_approaches: Letting every specialist commit independently to the shared candidate, causing repeated CI cancellation/restart.
Treating all code changes as the same test/risk class.
Writing hot shared closure files throughout development instead of once at closure.
